name: Heatbugs
miniText: How can individual temperature preferences generate collective spatial patterns? NetLogo Heatbugs places heat-producing agents on a grid with heat diffusion and cooling. Uncomfortable bugs seek warmer or cooler unoccupied neighboring cells, with occasional random movement. The scientific context is an artificial-agent platform demonstration [1,2] and the problem of aligning implementations [3], rather than a species-specific biological theory. The Info explicitly says that rigorous equivalence with Swarm and Repast was not established. Heterogeneous preferences, occupancy constraints, and field dynamics can produce clusters or avoidance. These are outcomes of the specified artificial rules; they do not establish biological thermoregulation, physical calibration of heat units, or verified equivalence among toolkit versions.
